set.body:
Phase B (assurance floor; gates Phase D). This is the largest single assurance gap in the repository.

Current state, measured across all 57 test files under modules/*/src/test:
  forAll: 0
  Gen. / Arbitrary / Cogen: 0
  checkAll / RuleSet / discipline: 0
  import org.scalacheck.* / Prop: 0
  extends ScalaCheckSuite: 0
Every suite extends munit.CatsEffectSuite (31) or munit.FunSuite (24).

ScalaCheck IS a declared dependency of every module (project/Dependencies.scala:13,26,28; build.sbt:20-21) and has never been used. discipline-munit, cats-laws and discipline-core are NOT dependencies at all.

This contradicts recorded commitments in docs/plans/2026-07-23-site-layer.md:53-55 ("any new Eq/Order/Monoid instance ships with a discipline law test (checkAll)") and :60 ("Every new codec ships a round-trip property test (ScalaCheck, finally used)").

Fix:
- Add discipline-munit and cats-laws.
- Generators for the identifier and evidence surface.
- The first four law families, in the review's priority order: attribution; submission and cancellation uncertainty; evidence monotonicity; result authority.
- Test unknown-field preservation ONLY for envelopes that explicitly promise it.

Ordering rationale: the review placed laws at P2, AFTER all architecture. That inverts their purpose. Phase D rewrites the submission path, the state model and job identity simultaneously; these properties are the net under that work and are worth far less written afterwards. Remaining law families (journal replay/epoch fencing, atomic publication, batch bijection/sharding, protocol fragmentation) follow in Phase E alongside codec ownership.
set.title: P8.B2: Add discipline and the first four law families
